section.title: Urban beekeeping
section.text:
Urban beekeeping

A. Twenty years ago, few people kept bees in cities. Today, rooftop hives can be found in many European capitals, and some city councils even offer training courses for beginners.

B. Supporters argue that urban hives help to pollinate parks and gardens. In one study in a northern city, fruit trees within 500 metres of a hive produced 20% more fruit than trees further away.

C. However, ecologists warn that too many hives may harm wild bees, which compete with honeybees for the same flowers. In the author's view, cities should count their hives before encouraging more of them.

D. Honey produced in cities is often surprisingly clean. Tests show that bees filter many pollutants, so city honey can be as pure as honey from the countryside.

groups.instruction: Choose the correct heading for paragraphs A and B.
